slides.title: MDF++: Visuo-Tactile World Action Model with End-to-end Representation Learning
slides.highlight: MDF++ introduces a visuo-tactile world action model that learns control-relevant representations end-to-end using a diffusion backbone, outperforming models with frozen encoders by up to 50% on contact-rich manipulation tasks.

card.one_liner: MDF++ learns task-aware visuo-tactile representations end-to-end for contact-rich robot manipulation.
card.key_idea: Jointly trains observation encoders with a diffusion world-action model using selective gradient flow to prevent feature collapse.
card.evaluation: Tested on five simulated and two real-world threading tasks; outperforms frozen-encoder baselines by up to 50% success rate.
card.limitation: Requires manual loss weight tuning per modality and processes force signals at low frequency, missing high-frequency dynamics.

slides.title: Learning Heterogeneous Tactile Representation for General Dexterous Manipulation
slides.tldr: UNIFIED TACTILE REPRESENTATION FOR DEXTEROUS MANIPULATION
slides.highlight: This work introduces a tactile foundation model that creates unified representations across heterogeneous sensors, enhancing dexterous manipulation capabilities relevant to embodied AI research.

card.one_liner: LingBot-Touch unifies heterogeneous tactile sensor data into plug-and-play tokens for enhanced dexterous manipulation.
card.key_idea: Develops a tactile foundation model creating unified representations across diverse sensors, seamlessly integrating into diffusion and VLA policies.
card.evaluation: Validated via simulation and real-robot experiments across multiple platforms, showing improved dexterity and efficiency over baselines.

slides.title: PCTac: Mechanochromic Photonic-Crystal Tactile Sensor for Dexterous Manipulation
slides.highlight: This work introduces PCTac, an open-source tactile sensor using mechanochromic photonic-crystal materials to encode contact load directly as a spatially resolved hue field. By integrating this structural-color representation into Diffusion Policy, the sensor achieves higher success rates in dexterous manipulation tasks compared to standard RGB tactile and vision-only baselines.

card.one_liner: PCTac uses mechanochromic photonic crystals to encode contact stress directly as hue for robot learning.
card.key_idea: A tactile fingertip converts local stress into spatially resolved structural color, using reference-relative hue maps as direct policy observations.
card.evaluation: Tested on three real-robot tasks with Diffusion Policy; PCTac Hue achieved 75.6% success, outperforming RGB and vision-only baselines.
card.limitation: Low sensitivity to concave features and ambiguity in distinguishing normal versus shear stress responses due to material properties.

slides.title: Which Taxels, Not How Many: Tactile Sensor Placement for Dexterous Policies
slides.highlight: This study demonstrates that strategic tactile sensor placement based on contact statistics significantly outperforms uniform distribution, offering insights into efficient multimodal perception design relevant to HyECHO's goal of non-data-hungry state observation.

card.one_liner: Strategic tactile sensor placement based on contact statistics outperforms uniform placement with fewer taxels.
card.key_idea: Selects taxels using teacher policy contact statistics (Top-contact/Cover) rather than uniform distribution, isolating placement effects via controlled distillation.
card.evaluation: Simulated in-palm rotation and grasping on three hands; metrics include success rate and held fraction; compared against uniform, link-proportional, and least-contact baselines.
card.limitation: Results are simulation-only; sensor noise and drift are untested; placement benefits vary by task, with contact coverage mattering more than concentration in grasping.

slides.title: Tactile Sensors Are an Effective Substitute for Wrist Cameras in Contact-Rich or Occluded Manipulation
slides.tldr: TACTILE SENSING OUTPERFORMS WRIST CAMERAS IN CONTACT-RICH MANIPULATION
slides.highlight: This study demonstrates that finger-mounted tactile sensors can significantly outperform wrist cameras in contact-rich manipulation tasks, offering a robust solution for handling occluded or hidden contacts. This aligns with MOSAIC's focus on physics and force-based estimation for procedural skill assessment in complex assembly scenarios.

card.one_liner: Finger-mounted tactile sensors outperform wrist cameras in contact-rich or occluded robot manipulation tasks.
card.key_idea: Integrates low-cost tactile arrays into an ACT policy, replacing wrist cameras with scene/egocentric vision plus touch for contact feedback.
card.evaluation: Tested on six real-world tasks with 1,000 rollouts; tactile policies significantly outperformed wrist-camera vision-only baselines on contact-rich tasks.
card.limitation: Results limited to one robot platform, sensor type, policy architecture, and training seed; tactile gains vary by task visibility.

slides.title: Robust Readout of Cross-Point Resistive Arrays via Time-Domain Optimization
slides.tldr: TIME-DOMAIN OPTIMIZATION FOR ROBUST TACTILE SENSING
slides.highlight: This work introduces a time-domain optimization method for cross-point resistive arrays that significantly improves readout robustness against noise and long interconnects, offering a more reliable approach for high-density tactile sensing in robotics.

card.one_liner: Time-domain waveform fitting improves robustness of cross-point resistive array readout under noise.
card.key_idea: Replaces spectral amplitude extraction with nonlinear least-squares fitting of time-domain current waveforms to estimate resistances.
card.evaluation: Simulated 16x16 arrays in LTspice; reduced mean error by 24.6% and standard deviation by 77.6% versus FFT baseline under noise.
card.limitation: Higher computational cost due to iterative optimization; ignores sneak-path currents inherent to cross-point arrays.

slides.title: On Agentic Manipulation Policies
slides.tldr: GENERALIST AGENTS OUTPERFORM SPECIALIST MANIPULATION POLICIES
slides.highlight: This paper demonstrates that generalist AI agents can control manipulators more reliably than specialist policies, adapting strategies and utilizing persistent memory to learn from experience. This aligns with ADAM-CHAT's focus on test-time adaptation and meta-cognitive self-correction for robust human-AI teaming.

card.one_liner: Generalist AI models controlling robots directly outperform specialist policies in zero-shot manipulation tasks.
card.key_idea: AMP1 harness lets frontier models command manipulators directly via code and vision, adapting strategies in real-time without predefined skills.
card.evaluation: State-of-the-art results on RoboLab-120 (85.6%) and real-world trials (96.3%), surpassing VLA/WAM baselines with no task-specific training.
card.limitation: High latency due to model reasoning time; performance heavily depends on the underlying generalist model's spatial cognition capabilities.

slides.title: SURE: Spatiotemporal Uncertainty Representation for Efficient Vision-Language-Action Learning
slides.highlight: SURE addresses spatiotemporal uncertainty in robot manipulation by modeling spatial and temporal variations in demonstration data, enabling efficient Vision-Language-Action learning with significantly reduced data requirements.

card.one_liner: SURE improves VLA data efficiency by modeling spatial and temporal action uncertainty via probabilistic decoding and Soft-DTW.
card.key_idea: Combines a transposed-convolutional probabilistic action decoder for spatial uncertainty with Soft-DTW alignment supervision for temporal robustness.
card.evaluation: Tested on LIBERO, RoboTwin 2.0, and real-world tasks; outperforms OpenVLA-OFT with 10-20% of data or steps.
card.limitation: Requires careful hyperparameter tuning for Soft-DTW smoothing and KL regularization; real-world success rates remain moderate (~57%).
